content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Compare renewable and non-renewable energy resources
Describe the advantages and disadvantages of different energy sources
Explain the chemistry of fossil fuels and biofuels
Discuss the future of energy and the transition to sustainable sources
Energy is essential for modern life, but our current reliance on
is unsustainable. Understanding the chemistry of different
helps us evaluate options for a sustainable energy future.
Buried and compressed over millions of years
Heat and pressure converted to fuel
Heat used to generate steam → electricity
Intermittent, land use, energy to manufacture
Reliable, can store energy, no emissions
Less energy per litre than petrol
~80% of global energy from fossil fuels
Need to reduce to limit climate change
Compare the environmental impacts of using coal versus wind power for electricity generation.
Releases CO₂ when burned (causes climate change)
Produces SO₂ and NOₓ (cause acid rain)
Wind has much lower overall environmental impact
Wind is renewable; coal will run out
But wind needs backup for when wind doesn't blow
Explain why bioethanol is considered carbon neutral.
Plants absorb CO₂ from atmosphere by photosynthesis
Carbon is stored in the plant
Some CO₂ released, but offset by absorption
CO₂ released when burned = CO₂ absorbed during growth
Net addition of CO₂ to atmosphere is zero
But much better than fossil fuels
Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of hydrogen as a fuel.
Can power vehicles and heat buildings
Currently mostly made from natural gas (not green)
Difficult to store (very light, needs high pressure)
Hydrogen could be important for decarbonising transport and industry
But only if made using renewable electricity ("green hydrogen")
Challenges of storage and infrastructure need solving
Depends on how it's made; most is currently from natural gas
Thinking biofuels are perfectly carbon neutral
Energy for production means not perfectly neutral
Assuming renewables can replace fossil fuels immediately
Transition requires storage, grid changes, time
High energy but cause climate change, will run out
Low carbon but radioactive waste, high cost
Solar, wind, hydro - clean but intermittent
Made from plants, potentially carbon neutral
Clean when burned, but production matters
Moving from fossil fuels to renewables
Understanding fuels and developing new solutions
